The statement as data: every verdict of a regression or property proof carries what it is about, its domain, assumptions with their basis, observations, bounds, models, checker, gap mode and confirmation, and the page states it (verification pending)

Vacuity as a status: a verified regression or property proof says whether it is about any input, non-vacuous (with the probe's witness), vacuous or unknown, and a proof over records says the constructors' agreement is another obligation (verification pending)

The gap protocol: under --gaps advised a proof that reaches a gap of the tool's own checker with no contract stops before solving, and returns each gap with what a contract for it must state and a template

Contracts for gaps: under --gaps advised, --contracts FILE gives the tool's own checker a contract per gap, which it applies at the call in place of the gap, refuses with the reason when it cannot, and names in the verdict as trusted

Contracts tested on a real JVM: each contract for a gap is run against the JDK's own call on boundary and seeded random inputs before the tool's own checker applies it; one the JVM refutes goes back to the agent with its counterexamples, and the verdict counts its contracts as tested or trusted

Calls whose value a proof reads are gaps: a JDK method returning a primitive and a static JDK method the tool's own checker does not model are named gaps with no assume form, which a contract closes by stating the result, tested on a real JVM

Contracts proved against the JDK's bytecode: a contract for a static JDK method of primitives is proved by the tool's own checker running the JDK's own class, the strongest evidence level, and a proof that refutes one hands its input to the JVM test

The advised mode recorded end to end: two Crosscut examples, an agent's contract the JVM refutes going back to it, and a proof that closes on one contract proved against the JDK's bytecode and two tested (verification pending)

The contract library: contracts for gaps of the tool's own checker, checked once against the JDK's bytecode or on a real JVM and recorded, which a run under --gaps advised applies without checking them again, and --max-trust to refuse trusted ones (verification pending)

The verify-bytecode skill closes gaps with contracts: its proofs run under --gaps advised --max-trust 0, it writes a contract for each JDK call the tool's own checker does not implement, corrects one the JVM refutes, reports each contract's evidence level, and offers the ones that held for the contract library

A witness found through contracts is run on a real JVM: the harness the checker proved, with the JDK's own calls where the contracts stood, makes it a violation when it fails there and no verdict when it holds

JBMC's interval stages run only where they bound an input, and a check has one deadline: a harness over arrays alone, as example 142's, runs JBMC once, and every run gets a budget out of --timeout (verification pending)

JBMC is read through --json-ui, and every run says how it ended: a counterexample, an unwinding failure, a timeout, memory exhausted, a solver failure or an input JBMC refused stay apart, with the text reader kept until a differential test over the recorded JBMC examples agrees (verification pending)

JBMC's own approximations are gaps under strict and assume: its stubs of methods it has no bytecode for, the invokedynamic call sites it gives the value zero or null, and the monitors it drops are named from its goto program, and a JBMC proof that reaches one is no verdict under strict (verification pending)

JBMC applies the contracts for its gaps: under --engine jbmc --gaps advised a JDK call JBMC stubs takes the contract the own checker would, its call sites rewritten into calls of the contract's method, and a gap with no contract stops the run with the advice

The benchmark corpus: the conformance corpus, four documented bugs with their broken and fixed versions, and twelve held-out regressions, run on both engines under strict, assume and advised, with every expected answer and every witness checked on the JVM and correctness, coverage, time and memory kept apart (verification pending)

Per-phase measurements for both engines: every checker run split into loading, lowering, symbolic execution, encoding, solving and trace, with its formula's size, JBMC's read from its own timings and message times, and a table per workload of which phase dominates (verification pending)
